analysis.title: US Software: AI Positioning, Agentic Security, Midterm Implications (Software Playbook)
key_insights: Citi says software remains investable but the burden of proof for AI tailwinds has risen after a volatile Q3 earnings season. Sustained re-ratings now require meaningful improvement in growth expectations with enough disclosure to validate AI tailwinds.

Citi prefers the infrastructure, data and security layers, where AI workloads translate more directly into consumption and revenue. Top ideas: MDB, SNOW, ESTC (Radke, Wong), NET, TEAM, DDOG (Boolani, Zhang), BOX, NAVN, ROP (Enders, Kurosawa).

Application software is a selective call. Citi favors names with proprietary data, domain expertise, regulatory value, strong distribution and a credible AI upsell or consumption path. It prefers companies with consistent execution because of enterprise deal-cycle delays.

AI disruption of traditional search is hurting customer acquisition in SMB and self-service software. Citi is incrementally cautious on names leveraged to search channels. Most exposed: MNDY, ASAN, INTU, DBX, HUBS, ADBE, GTM, FIG.

Post-midterm ('blue sweep') concerns about data-center permitting and power use are seen as mainly a sentiment and positioning risk. Citi expects AI demand and the data-center buildout to continue. Owners of existing capacity (MSFT, ORCL, DOCN, NET) could see that capacity valued higher.

Sub-scale neoclouds are the most exposed to the midterm policy risk. Slower permitting and higher financing costs are the larger headwind. Citi expects unsecured and convertible borrowing to get harder, with secured and ATM issuance more common, and costs likely passed on to customers.
Application software could see rotational benefit if sentiment headwinds linger, and a valuation tailwind if inflation expectations cool and long-term rates fall.

AI-assisted vulnerability discovery (PHP2Shell) is raising security concerns, but Citi's CISO org conversations indicate such headlines will not cause a budget flush. They push a lasting shift toward hardening security estates, expanding the 'AI for Security' and 'Security for AI' opportunity.

Q3 read-through: NOW (-27%), TEAM (-16%), DDOG (-14%) are judged largely idiosyncratic. FIG (-17%) and BL (-23%) show more symptomatic issues: top-of-funnel weakness in front-office apps and rising budget and governance scrutiny. NET (+10%) benefited from AI/agent adoption.

NOW's miss came from lower Q4 cRPO guidance (early renewals, more on-prem deals, termination-for-convenience contracts not counted in cRPO). Citi says the rebucketing of subscription revenue into professional services with more forward-deployed engineers could be symptomatic of enterprise apps struggling to show value.

M&A is providing valuation support as strategics buy AI, data, security and workflow assets. Possible acquirers: CRM, NOW, ADBE, INTU, TEAM. Recent deals: IonQ/Elisity ($1.3B), DT/Arize ($915M), PANW/Console ($500M), CRWD/Dreadnode and Fiddler AI ($500M), and a reported DDOG bid for Upwind.
Takeout candidates: ESTC, SMWB, DOCU, KVYO, AMPL (apps/data); DT, PRGS, RPD (infrastructure); SPSC, BL, VERX, PAYC, PCTY, WK (back office).

Apps/data: MSFT and ORCL are top AI Defense names. Vertical software (ADSK, GWRE, VEEV) is most defensive. Hyperscalers/neoclouds (MSFT, ORCL, CRWV) and data names (SNOW, MDB, ESTC) have the best AI positioning. Most cautious on SMWB, AMPL, GTM and CXM.

Front-office apps: Citi is cautious on top-of-funnel impacts and sees greatest risk at sell-rated GTM and ADBE, with neutral ratings on HUBS and CRM. It is upbeat on B2C/e-commerce names SHOP and KVYO (agentic commerce). In customer service, NICE and CXM are viewed more cautiously, while buy-rated ZM benefits from a cleaner architecture and lower price point.
MDB has growth acceleration driven by 150%+ growth in AI-native Atlas. SNOW is re-accelerating toward 40%+ growth. ESTC could accelerate toward 20%+ revenue growth.

Back office: BOX and APPN are the most favored for sustained AI-driven acceleration. BOX's Enterprise Advanced upsell drives a 30-40% price uplift. Citi is most cautious on DBX, MNDY and ASAN, though it keeps Buy or Buy/HR ratings on INTU, MNDY and ASAN on offsetting factors and dislocated valuation.

NAVN has record bookings, $4B of TTM new gross bookings (+60% y/y) and a proprietary-AI cost advantage. ROP's organic growth accelerated to 7% y/y in Q3 from 5% in Q2 with a beat-and-raise, and it has $6B+ of dry powder for M&A.

Infrastructure software: NET, DDOG, CRWD, ZS and PANW screen best on combined AI defense and offense. Citi sees ZS (-14% YTD per its table, cited as -25% in text) as a tactical dislocation. It is most cautious on RPD and FSLY (share-loss risk).

NET is a top idea: ~150k+ paying customer additions (+96% QoQ), record revenue, and early revenue from 'Act IV' agent-economy products, with agentic traffic outpacing human traffic and visibility into 20%+ of world web traffic.
TEAM trades at about 6x EV/S and 19x NTM EV/FCF, below its 3-year and 5-year medians. Citi sees the weak guidance reaction as a buying opportunity ahead of Rovo AI monetization.

DDOG: Citi views the stock's focus on mega-customer usage rationalization as overshadowing healthy broader momentum. Infrastructure monitoring is at $2B+ ARR growing over 30%. Short-term headwinds (renewals, weak Q4 guide, tough 1H27 comps) likely keep shares rangebound.

Consumption-model debate: DDOG, NET, SNOW and to a lesser extent DT have seen growth inflect, but concentration in AI-native customers raises optimization risk, similar to the post-COVID hangover. Citi treats DDOG's guide as noisy and idiosyncratic.

earnings_insights: NOW reported Q3 on 10/29/26 and the stock fell 27%. Q4 cRPO guidance was below expectations because of early renewals, more on-prem deals and termination-for-convenience contracts excluded from cRPO. Subscription revenue was also rebucketed into professional services.
FIG reported Q3 on 11/4/26 and fell 17%. New customer adds across $10K+ and $100K+ ARR cohorts slowed y/y and q/q, a trend also seen in the HUBS and KVYO Q3 reports.

TEAM reported on 11/6/26 and fell 16%. Hybrid deals shifted Cloud vs Data Center revenue allocation in the quarter, and a relatively new CFO is guiding conservatively with three quarters left in the fiscal year.
DDOG reported on 11/4/26 and fell 14%. The weak Q4 guide and renewal dynamics center on largest-customer usage rationalization. Infrastructure monitoring is at $2B+ ARR growing over 30%.
NET reported on 11/6/26 and rose 10%. Workers developer platform workload growth from AI/agents drove the quarter, with ~150k+ paying customer additions (+96% QoQ).
BL reported on 11/6/26 and fell 23%. Q3 deal delays reflect rising budget and governance scrutiny of AI-enabled solutions, with more approval gates beyond the controller org.
ROP Q3: organic growth of 7% y/y versus 5% in Q2 (+2pt acceleration), with a DEPS beat-and-raise and stabilization at Deltek and DAT.
NAVN: $4B of TTM new gross bookings (+60% y/y), record bookings and a new largest customer.
MNDY Q3 and HUBS Q3 calls and the ASAN FQ2 10-Q all cite reduced reliance on traditional search and pressure on top-of-funnel and self-serve demand.

vol_and_positioning: Citi says post-midterm data-center policy concerns are more likely to create near-term sentiment and positioning risk than to change long-term AI demand.
Citi's quantitative research crowding scores accompany the sub-sector sentiment charts. A higher score means more crowding.
Citi sees DDOG shares rangebound near term because of renewal dynamics, a weak Q4 guide and tough 1H27 comps.
geopolitical: Midterm elections ('blue sweep') have raised concerns about data-center permitting, power-consumption scrutiny and possible limits on the pace of AI infrastructure expansion.

PHP2Shell, a PHP remote-code-injection vulnerability found with Gemini Argon and an unreleased frontier model, took down many government agency and public-facing websites until edge security vendors patched within 24 hours.

tension_points.bull_case: AI demand, cloud migration and workloads are durable, and infrastructure under construction plus existing capacity limit the near-term impact. Existing owners (MSFT, ORCL, DOCN, NET) gain.
tension_points.bear_case: Tighter permitting, power scrutiny and higher financing costs could slow AI infrastructure expansion, hitting sub-scale neoclouds hardest.

tension_points.bull_case: AI-assisted vulnerability discovery and agentic attack surfaces expand the 'AI for Security' and 'Security for AI' TAM.
tension_points.bear_case: Budgeting cycles and procurement timelines mean headlines do not translate into immediate spending, and frontier labs (Daybreak, Glasswing, Gemini Cyber) may encroach.

tension_points.theme: agentic AI at the app layer
tension_points.bull_case: Agentic systems sold on top of existing systems of record show early adoption and monetization (BL, INTU, MANH, ROP).
tension_points.bear_case: Agentic AI could replace categories of enterprise application software, and growth inflections remain early.

tension_points.bull_case: DDOG, NET, SNOW and DT growth is tethered to AI adoption and benefits from being in the path of tokenization.
tension_points.bear_case: Concentration in hyper-growth AI-natives raises spending optimization risk, similar to the post-COVID hangover that decelerated DDOG.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A repeat of the post-COVID-style optimization seen in 2027 usage austerity, which Citi frames as the open question of whether 2027 sees austerity.

tension_points.bull_case: Offsets exist in upmarket pivots, alternative channels and existing-customer expansion, with modest traffic recovery noted at ASAN.
tension_points.bear_case: AI is disrupting traditional search discovery, with MNDY, HUBS and ASAN guiding to continued pressure.
